scope: Recovery checkout on audit/resume-huellitas. Before and after scans both include the existing test-tooling and React DOM manifest/lock changes; only the transitive shell-quote lock entry changed between these scans. No hosted service or production deployment was audited.

audit.exitCodeNote: Yarn audit returns a severity bitmask. Exit 14 is the expected low/moderate/high finding result, not a scan failure.
audit.countingNote: auditPathEntries count repeated registry findings across dependency paths. Distinct GHSA URLs count separate advisories. Neither number is a count of demonstrated application exploits. A registry advisory can have multiple version-specific numeric IDs.

change.method: Remove only the shell-quote@^1.6.1 lock stanza; run pinned Yarn 1.22.22 install --ignore-scripts --non-interactive, then verify the lock diff.
change.lockOnlyDiff: Only shell-quote version, resolved URL, and integrity changed relative to the pre-refresh lockfile.

limitations: Classification is a source and dependency-chain triage, not a complete exploitability analysis, native-bundle inspection, penetration test, or production verification.
Expo/React Native list much of their toolchain under ordinary dependencies. Yarn dev=false and its dependency count do not establish mobile runtime reachability.
Build tools and development servers can process untrusted input or be exposed on a network. Tooling classification does not mean a vulnerability is harmless.

Registry audit covers declared package versions; it does not reliably detect vendored or prebundled copies. react-devtools-core standalone still embeds an older shell-quote parser, so this refresh is not proof that all DevTools code has been patched.

The shell-quote critical advisory requires an attacker-controlled object .op value to reach quote() and shell execution. No such Huellitas execution path was found; resolving the registry finding does not demonstrate a previously exploitable mobile critical issue.
Some packages have no fixed version recorded for the installed line. A patchedRange of <0.0.0 in registry details means no available patched range, not an installable target.

No Expo/React Native SDK, Metro, navigation, signing, or other major dependency upgrade was attempted in this bounded recovery patch. Remaining findings require a separate supported-SDK upgrade and compatibility/security review.

packageExposureAssessments.assessment: Expo plist/XML processing dependencies; no Huellitas application import identified.
Glob/minimatch chains in React Native and Expo tools.
Metro/micromatch file matching; no patched range reported by the registry for the installed line.
Expo CLI HTTP compression; exposure depends on whether a developer server is reachable.

Present through Expo Router/React Navigation/query-string. React Navigation upstream has a parse path, but the installed Expo Router fork uses URL.searchParams for its main incoming query parser. No Huellitas exploit demonstrated; 0.5.0 is outside the current ^0.2.2 requirement.
Metro image/asset processing; malformed build inputs matter. A forced major update requires compatibility validation.
React Navigation/Expo Router and PostCSS use this package. Inspected navigation calls use default sizes, rather than attacker-controlled zero/negative sizes involved in these reports.
Expo signing/certificate tooling; no patched range reported for the installed line.
Expo web CSS processing, including source maps.

react-native > react-devtools-core > shell-quote. The React Native integration is under __DEV__ and loads the backend entry. The standalone DevTools bundle includes an older parser used for local REACT_EDITOR handling; updating this separately installed package does not rewrite that embedded bundle.
Jest/js-yaml formatting chain; no patched range reported for the installed line.
xcode tooling chain; the reported fix requires a major-line change.

Present through Supabase Realtime and developer servers. The installed Realtime factory prefers a native global WebSocket when available, as on React Native/browser; installation alone does not establish use of the Node ws implementation in the mobile app.
